concepts.label: ep-engine worker thread pool (reader/writer/auxio/nonio)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted earlier in this batch on cbstats-dispatcher-job.json; reused here since ep_workload:num_readers/num_writers/num_auxio/num_nonio/num_shards/num_sleepers/ready_tasks describe the same four-way thread pool's current sizing and load

concepts.label: ep-engine per-thread-kind priority task queue
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the LowPrioQ_AuxIO/LowPrioQ_NonIO/LowPrioQ_Reader/LowPrioQ_Writer InQsize/OutQsize pairs describe a distinct mechanism from the thread pool itself: a per-thread-kind input/output queue holding tasks waiting to run or having completed. No existing concept represents a scheduler-side task queue; kept at this single mechanism level rather than minting one concept per queue name

relations.subject: monitoring:ep-engine-thread-pool
relations.evidence: The vBucket map for the bucket is grouped into multiple vBuckets, where one read worker accesses one of the vBuckets.

relations.subject: monitoring:ep-engine-thread-pool
relations.evidence: This command is used to check how many threads of various types are currently running.

notable_absence.finding: ep_workload:num_shards and the reader-to-vBucket-group mapping describe a sharding mechanism (each reader owns a group of vBuckets) that has no dedicated concept anywhere in the registry excerpt beyond the already-promoted server:vbucket itself - there is no concept for the SHARD (the group of vBuckets one worker owns) as distinct from the vBucket. Left as evidence/prose in the reliesOnMechanism relation above rather than minted, since one page's one sentence is too thin a basis to name a new mechanism-level concept for it.

cross_component_finding: This is the one page in the batch where the ep-engine-internals vocabulary genuinely does connect to an already-promoted, non-internals concept: num_readers/num_writers/num_auxio/num_nonio directly correspond to the reader/writer/auxio/nonio categories in cbstats-dispatcher-job.md and cbstats-tasks.md, and the reader-worker-to-vBucket sharding sentence ties the thread pool directly to server:vbucket - a real overlap point, contradicting a literal reading of 'least vocabulary overlap of any batch' for this specific page even though the batch as a whole still shows unusually little overlap.
cross_product_finding: None - this page is Couchbase Server CLI-only with no Capella-facing surface.
